# To the
## Honorable, Greatly Respected, and Highly Distinguished Gentleman
# Wilhelm Stadtländer,
### Distinguished Citizen and Merchant in Hamburg, etc.
### Our Greatly Gracious and Highly Honored Lord!

## Highly Honored Sir,

Although that part of <term>Natural Wisdom</term><note>A historical term for "Natural Philosophy," the study of the physical world and the precursor to modern science.</note> which deals with the transformation of metals is held in poor regard by almost everyone—even by many among the learned themselves who devote themselves to the investigation of nature and undertake to teach its secrets to others—this is partly because this art seems entirely incomprehensible to them and contrary to their <term>Aristotelian Philosophy</term><note>The traditional academic framework based on the teachings of Aristotle, which many alchemists felt was too theoretical and failed to account for experimental chemical changes.</note>. Furthermore, exceedingly few are found who can actually and in deed demonstrate those things of which those who have written of this wisdom speak and boast so much. It is also partly because daily many rogue <term>Sophists</term><note>In the context of alchemy, "sophists" or "puffers" were fraudulent practitioners who used trickery and false promises of gold-making to deceive wealthy patrons.</note> and impostors appear here and there under the name of "Philosophers," who through cunning malice and schemes, with great boasting, swearing, and assumed...

<summary>This page is a formal dedication to Wilhelm Stadtländer, a prominent Hamburg merchant. The author defends alchemy (the "transformation of metals") against its contemporary critics and distinguishes true "Natural Wisdom" from the fraudulent practices of impostors.</summary>

<keywords>Dedication, Wilhelm Stadtländer, Hamburg, Natural Philosophy, Alchemical Theory, Aristotelianism, Sophists, Metal Transformation</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the dedication to Wilhelm Stadtländer. The previous page ended mid-sentence, describing how fraudsters use "assumed..." (angenommener) to deceive others. feigned hypocrisy, lead and place many people of high and low status into great and powerful expense, damage, mockery, and ruin; nevertheless (to say nothing of current experience and visual proof, of which irrefutable examples exist in all times, even our own), there have at all times, in all places of the world, and among all nations, been found excellent and credible people who have diligently researched this noble art with rational disregard for all biased judgments. Through the blessing of the Most High, and untiring diligence, effort, and labor, they have reached the goal set forth therein. Subsequently, they left it behind in their writings, unanimously confirmed through such immovable arguments firmly grounded in Nature herself, that to accuse them all, without distinction, of lies and folly would itself be a great folly and irresponsible malice. 

And it is, indeed, an absurd conclusion to claim that because someone does not know, understand, or cannot grasp this or that, or has not seen it themselves, or because some fraudsters make this <term>secret science</term><note>The author uses "Wissenschafft" here to mean a systematic body of knowledge, specifically the "hermetic science" or alchemy.</note> suspicious, that the same must not be consistent with truth, or cannot be found in nature at all, or is even vain lies and deception, and therefore to be rejected entirely.

...greatest use in the healing of severe diseases and those abandoned by others / used primarily for the comfort and refreshment of the poor / and so that such a high treasure and heartfelt gift from the Most High would not remain buried with him / but might instead fruitfully serve posterity / he explained and described the preparation of such mysteries in his excellent writings / so thoroughly and extensively / yet according to the secret and customary usage of the **Sages** <note>The "Sages" or "Wise Men" refers to the long tradition of alchemists who used metaphorical language to protect their secrets.</note> / that these same [writings] are rightly loved by many intelligent and truth-loving people above all others / highly valued / diligently searched / and read with special benefit and pleasure.

Which then gave us the occasion and moved us / to diligently collect his writings, as many as were to be obtained / to look through them / to replace and improve the defects and deficiencies found in previous *editions* <note>original: "editionen"</note> / and to have everything brought together in this convenient form.

# Preface.
# Containing the reason for this edition, and an Encomium <note>A formal piece of writing that highly praises someone or something; a tribute.</note>
### Of the Writings
# OF BROTHER BASIL VALENTINE,

Saint Augustine writes that the most distinguished study of all philosophers <note>original: *Philosophorum*</note> was this: namely, how one might live happily and well in the world / which happiness is called the highest good <note>original: *Summum bonum*</note> or the most noble and exalted good. ( *Augustine, On the Epicureans and Stoics* <note>original: *Aug. de Epicur. & Stoic.*</note> )

Now, this title belongs alone to the eternal and almighty / triune invisible **GOD** / for He is the true highest good <note>original: *summum bonum*</note>.

According to worldly understanding, however, our ancient <term>Philosopher's Stone</term> <note>The legendary "Lapis Philosophorum," believed to transform base metals into gold and serve as a universal medicine.</note> can likewise be called the highest good <note>original: *summum bonum*</note>.

For / as is written in the *Book of the Revelation of Hermes* <note>original: *Libro Apocalypseos Hermetis*; referring to Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary father of the Hermetic and alchemical tradition.</note> / this work is the final / greatest

It frames the alchemical pursuit within the context of Saint Augustine's writings on happiness and the classical philosophical tradition.</summary>

# Preface

...discovered that all natural things wish to reveal themselves; for this reason, He <note>Referring to God, the Creator.</note> has primarily shown us that even heavenly things are made naturally, so that through them His infinite and unsearchable power and wisdom might be better recognized.

All of this the Philosophers have seen in the light of nature <note>original: "Liecht der Natur." This refers to the "Lumen Naturae," a concept popularized by Paracelsus suggesting that nature itself provides a divine internal guidance or illumination to those who study it.</note> as if in a mirror. Therefore, they held this science in such high esteem and wrote of it so sparingly and cautiously, and never otherwise than in figures, riddles, and parables <note>Alchemical texts were notoriously cryptic to prevent "unworthy" or greedy individuals from misuse of the "Great Work."</note>, so that such a Divine mystery—through which nature is discovered—would not be revealed to the unworthy. You yourself, Christian reader, if you could rightly know yourself and did not have a hardened understanding, might easily understand this—you who are created according to the likeness of the great world <note>The macrocosm/microcosm theory: the belief that the human body (microcosm) reflects the structure and laws of the entire universe (macrocosm).</note>, indeed, in the Image of God <note>original: "Ebenbild GOttes"</note>, as the Philosophers occasionally mention here and there.

Basil Valentine <note>A legendary 15th-century alchemist and Benedictine monk, often cited as a primary authority in later Hermetic traditions.</note> mentions in his writings a Mirror of Philosophical Wisdom.

Nicholas Flamel <note>A 14th-century French scribe who, according to legend, achieved the Great Work and lived for centuries. He is a central figure in alchemical lore.</note> writes in his preface on page 32: "Indeed, I would have had enough had I prepared the Philosophers' Stone but once; but my delight was too great in seeing and contemplating the wonders of nature within the vessels."

Again, Basil Valentine speaks of it in the Fifth Key <note>Referring to "The Twelve Keys of Basil Valentine," a famous set of alchemical instructions and allegories.</note> as follows:

"Thus you shall see and experience what the Creator and nature permit you to know; and know that I have made no further revelation with my mouth thus far, and God has [placed] more efficacy..." <note>The text breaks here; the German "Wir-" likely completes as "Wirckung" (efficacy or operation) on the following page.</note>

<summary>This page argues that nature is a reflection of God's wisdom and that alchemical secrets are intentionally hidden in riddles to protect them. It cites authorities like Basil Valentine and Nicholas Flamel to emphasize that the true joy of alchemy lies in witnessing the miraculous workings of nature.</summary>

<keywords>Light of Nature, Macrocosm, Microcosm, Image of God, Basil Valentine, Nicholas Flamel, Divine Mystery, Alchemy, Mirror of Wisdom, Fifth Key</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the Preface. The previous page discussed how the Philosophers' Stone reveals the world's secrets through the "Light of Nature." The text continues here mid-sentence, completing the word "Entdeckung" (discovery).</meta>

...covery and wonders of Nature incorporated, which many thousands of people cannot believe. To me, however, a seal is pre-imprinted <note>This implies the author feels divinely commissioned or "marked" to share this knowledge.</note>, so that others after me may also write of wondrous things which are naturally permitted by the Creator, but are held to be supernatural by the unwise; for the natural has its first beginning from the supernatural, and yet all is found to be nothing but sheer naturalness.

*Bernhardus Trevisanus* <note>Bernard of Treviso (1406–1490) was a famous Italian alchemist. His writings emphasized the "Great Work" as a spiritual and physical transformation.</note> in his preface sets down these words: "Thus the Art <note>original: "die Kunst." In this context, "The Art" specifically refers to Alchemy or the "Spagyric Art."</note> also adorns—when the composition of the true Stone <note>The Philosophers' Stone, the legendary substance capable of transmuting base metals into gold and granting eternal life or enlightenment.</note> is made—the person with such understanding that they rejoice within themselves and must thank and praise God with heartfelt desire for such a benefit."

In summary, this Art surpasses all other arts of this world, for it is a special gift of God and could well compel an evil rogue <note>original: "bösen Buben"</note> who might see it rightly to love God and turn away from his evil life. And therefore, it is not only very useful, but it shall also be used for nothing other than God's honor and the welfare of one's neighbor.

The aforementioned *Nicolaus Flamellus* <note>Nicolas Flamel (c. 1330–1418), a French scribe who, according to legend, succeeded in the alchemical Great Work. He was renowned for his supposed piety and philanthropy.</note> writes in his preface on page 35 of this Divine Work these words: "If the Stone is prepared by someone, it transforms the evil person into a pious one <note>original: "fremmen," an archaic form of "frommen" (devout/pious).</note> and roots out from them the root of all sin, which is avarice <note>original: "Geitz." Alchemy often teaches that the true Stone removes greed because the possessor has no need for worldly wealth.</note>, making them generous, gentle, pious, and God-fearing, however evil and perverse they may have been before."

<summary>The author concludes the preface by arguing that alchemy is a natural process rooted in the supernatural, serving as a divine gift that morally transforms the practitioner from a sinner into a pious, charitable soul.</summary>

# Preface

For henceforth he is, as it were, enraptured by the great grace and mercy that he has obtained from GOD, and by the depth of His divine, wondrous works.

> I have, dear reader, written these twelve small treatises for the benefit of the **children of the art**, so that before they grasp the work with their hands, they may learn to recognize the operations of **Nature**—specifically how she brings forth all things through her working—so that they do not try to enter the door without a key, or fetch water with a sieve. For he works in vain who attempts the labor in this holy and true art without knowledge of Nature; he is trapped in natural darkness, where the sun does not shine. He lies in thick shadow, where the moon does not shine at night.

We use these fires, and no more; the fire against nature must corrode the bodies <term>corpora: The physical substances or metals being worked upon.</term>. It is the **Dragon**, as I tell you, which burns more fiercely than the fires of hell.

The **natural fire** is the third **solvent** <term>Menstruum: A solvent or "catalyst" used to dissolve solid materials; in Ripley’s system, the "third menstruum" is a highly refined substance.</term>; this fire lies hidden within every thing. The accidental fire we call the **Unnatural**, such as the ash-fire <note>A method of indirect heating where the glass vessel is placed in a bed of hot ashes.</note> and the fire of the **bath** <term>Balnei: Short for *Balneum Mariae* or Mary’s Bath, a water bath used for gentle, steady heating.</term> for the purpose of **rotting** <note>original: *putreficiren*; Putrefaction is the stage where the matter decomposes and turns black, a necessary step before it can be purified.</note>. Without the aforementioned fire, you will bring nothing to rot, so that your **matter** <term>Materia</term> can be separated and made suitable for a new **joining** <term>Conjunction: The alchemical "marriage" or reuniting of the purified parts of the matter.</term>. Therefore, make your fire inside the glass, which burns the **bodies** <term>corpora</term> more fiercely than the elemental fire, if you wish to gain any benefit from our secret according to your heart's desire. Then your seed will rot and grow up with the help of the accidental fire, so that the same may afterwards be separated naturally.

Thus you must come through the **Gates of Separation**; then you can turn further toward the Gate of the **secret joining** <term>Conjunction</term>, which will lead you inside into the castle (take good note of this).

# Preface

...[at] ten o'clock set on fire, and in quick haste burned away everything I owned, so that I kept nothing in this world but my life, and might say with that philosopher: "All that is mine, I carry with me." <note>original Latin: *Omnia mea mecum porto*; a saying attributed to the Greek philosopher Bias of Priene, suggesting that true wealth lies in one's character and wisdom rather than physical possessions.</note>

In the fire, a **diamond ring** remained, which I had intended to give and honor my bride with. About five weeks after the fire, the golden ring was found again; however, the **diamond stone**, which had cost one hundred and forty-five **Reichsthaler** <term>Reichsthaler: A large silver coin used throughout the Holy Roman Empire; 145 thalers was a very significant sum, often exceeding the annual salary of a professional at the time.</term>, had sprung out because of the great heat and was judged to be lost. But finally, through the providence of **Almighty God**—who will not forsake those who fear Him, love Him, and rely upon Him—the little stone was found again in the first sieve when they began to wash the **dross** <term>dross: Original German *Krätze*, referring to the metallic waste, sweepings, or debris left over after a fire or smelting process.</term>. It had become more beautiful through the fire than it had been before; from this, I sensed that **God the Lord** wished to help me once more and to bless me.

To further describe the course of my life, I cannot leave the eager reader and seeker of the **art** <note>Refers to the "Hermetic Art" or alchemy.</note> uninformed that those who are to come to this high and great **secret** <note>The *Arcanum* or the mystery of the Philosopher's Stone.</note> are already foreseen and chosen by **GOD the LORD** from eternity, according to His great grace, love, and mercy, as the verses of **Johannis Ticinensis** <note>Johannes Ticinensis was a 14th-century Bohemian priest and alchemist whose rhythmic Latin verses were highly regarded by later seekers of the Stone.</note> state regarding this:

> The glowing **Stone** <note>original Latin: *Lapis candens*.</note> is made from three,
> To no one is it given, except to those
> To whom it comes by the **Breath of God** <note>original Latin: *DEI fit Spiramine*.</note>.

# Preface

...wishes to have, <note>This completes the thought from the previous page regarding the understanding of divine secrets.</note> it is clear and distinct enough for him, as **Basilius Valentinus** <note>A legendary 15th-century alchemist and Benedictine monk; his "Twelve Keys" is a foundational text of laboratory alchemy.</note> testifies on page 178 of his *Explanation of the Twelve Keys*.

In the year 1670, I promoted for print the little treatises of **John of Tetzen**, **Antonio of Abbatia**, and **Edward Kelley**; for these, I composed a preface. Therein, I warned all lovers of the secret and high Art against the **Sophists** <note>original: *Sophisten*; in an alchemical context, this refers to "puffers" or fraudsters who used false logic and deceptive chemical tricks rather than true philosophical principles.</note> and deceivers. I know best of all what promises the Sophists made to me; but a good angel warned me in time, so that I was not further deceived by them in any greater measure.

Now, I cannot neglect to further inform the lovers of this Art what kind of end such deceivers meet. I knew one—though not without loss to myself—who died in great poverty. On account of his debts, he was placed under arrest <note>A reference to the historical "arrest of the corpse," where creditors could legally prevent a burial until the deceased's debts were settled by the family.</note> in his own house even as he was to be buried; his daughter had to find a remedy if she wished to have him released.

<margin>I</margin> knew yet another among the **sellers of processes** <note>original: *Process Verkauffern*; those who made a living selling unverified or fraudulent alchemical recipes.</note> whom the righteous God caused to become bedridden while still having a healthy heart, so that he gradually had to sell and consume all his possessions. Thus, there is absolutely no blessing or prosperity from God found among such people who, with deceit and smooth words, misappropriate the sweat, goods, and blood of their neighbors.

# Concerning the Great Stone of the Ancient Sages / by Brother Basilius Valentinus of the Benedictine Order.

<image-desc>A large decorative initial 'I' within a square woodcut frame featuring floral and scrolling foliage motifs.</image-desc>

I have, in my preface / dear friend and devotee of the Art <term>Art</term> <note>original: *Kunst*; in this context, it refers to the "Great Art" of alchemy, the pursuit of the Philosopher's Stone.</note> / given promise / to you and others / who are eager / to learn the properties of Nature / and to research the arts from the heart / to show the cornerstone and rock / as much as has been permitted to me / and granted from above / from which our ancestors and the ancients / prepared their Stone / which they received from the Most High / to use for their health and the maintenance of this earthly life. So that I may now fulfill my promise and word / and not lead you astray into long-winded circuits through the errors of sophistry <term>sophistry</term> <note>original: *Sophisterey*; the author uses this to describe the deceptive or illogical practices of "false" alchemists who lacked true spiritual or chemical understanding.</note> / but rather reveal to you the main source of all goodness from its foundation.

Therefore you shall know / and take good heed of my following speech / if you otherwise desire to learn the Art / for I cannot provide much chatter / nor is it my intention / since the least is to be learned from it / but I love short words / that have a foundation within them.

The King's crown should be of pure gold, and a chaste bride shall be wedded to him. Therefore, if you wish to work through our bodies <note>In alchemical philosophy, "bodies" (German: *Cörper*) refer to the physical metallic substances being transformed.</note>, then take the greedy **gray wolf**, who on account of his name is subject to the bellicose **Mars** <note>original: "Marti"; the gray wolf is a symbol for antimony, which was often associated with iron (Mars) in chemical processing because iron was used to reduce the antimony ore.</note>. By birth, however, he is a child of old **Saturn** <note>original: "Saturni"; Saturn is the planetary symbol for lead, suggesting the heavy, metallic origins of the substance.</note>, who is found in the valleys and mountains of the world, and is possessed by a great hunger. Throw to him the body of the King, so that he may feed upon it. And when he has swallowed the King, then make a great fire and throw the wolf into it, so that he is consumed entirely; thus will the King be redeemed again. When this has happened three times, then the **Lion** has overcome the **Wolf**, and will find nothing more of him to consume; then our body is perfect for the beginning of our work.

And know that this alone is the right way, suitable for this purpose, to purify our bodies; for the **Lion** <note>original: "Leo"; the Lion often represents gold or the "fixed" principle that has been strengthened.</note> cleanses himself through the blood of the Wolf, and the blood's **tincture** <term>tincture|In alchemy, a tincture is a concentrated spiritual essence or medicinal "color" capable of permeating and transforming a substance.</term> rejoices marvelously with the tincture of the Lion, for the blood of both are in close kinship through their ancestry <note>original: "Gesipschafft"; this refers to the shared metallic nature of the materials.</note>. And when the Lion has been satiated, his spirit becomes stronger than before, and his eyes cast off a proud radiance, like the bright sun. His inner being is then capable of doing much, and is useful for all that is required of him; and when he is brought into his state of readiness, the children of men give thanks to him. Those burdened with heavy, falling sicknesses <note>German: "hinfallenden Kranckheiten"; a historical term for epilepsy.</note> and many plagues—the ten leprous men—run after him and desire to drink from the blood of his soul <note>original: "Seelen"; in this context, the "soul" of the metal refers to its most refined, liquid essence or "mercury."</note>, and all who have infirmities

## The Second Key.

IN the courts of the great and powerful, many kinds of drinks are found, and yet no two are alike in smell, color, and taste; for their preparation is varied, and yet they are all drunk, because each is prepared for its place and is necessary for the maintenance of the court.

When the sun gives off its rays and spreads them among the clouds, the common man says the sun is drawing water <note>A folk observation of crepuscular rays, which were often thought to be the sun physically pulling water up into the sky.</note> and it will rain; and if this happens often, it makes for a fruitful year. To build a precious, magnificent palace on high, many different types of masters and workers must lend their hands and be employed before the palace is adorned and can be called perfect. For what is meant to be stone cannot be made of wood.

# Of the Great Stone

<margin>

</margin>

does not burn, and yet it shines from afar. It does not give color either, unless it has first been prepared and is itself colored with its own hue, so that it may further color the weak, imperfect metals. However, this same **Sulfur** <note>original: "Schwebel," an archaic spelling of *Schwefel*. In alchemy, Sulfur represents the active, solar, and masculine principle of fire and soul.</note> is not permitted to color unless such color has been granted to it with great permanence. For the weak cannot triumph; rather, the stronger retains dominion over the weakest, and the weak must yield and give way to the strongest. Therefore, keep the following conclusion and meaning in mind regarding this discourse: a lowly thing cannot help another lowly thing, nor can it impart any advancement to its operation; and a combustible thing can provide no protection to another combustible thing to prevent it from burning. If a protector is to be present, one who dwells within the combustible and preserves it, then that protector must first have more power than the one he guards; he must previously have shown and proven himself in his own essence to be truly incombustible and constant. Thus, whoever wishes to prepare our incombustible **Sulfur** of all Sages should first take care to seek our Sulfur in something where it is inherently incombustible. The highest planet of the heavens, called **Saturn** <term>Saturn | in alchemy, this corresponds to the metal Lead; it represents the beginning of the work, associated with darkness, cold, and "base" matter</term>, has the least authority in our mastery, and yet he is the foremost **Key** of the entire Art. It then becomes such a malleable body as Saturn himself is, though subject to a much better constancy.

## The Eleventh Key. <insert>333 <unclear>reigned</unclear></insert>

The Eleventh Key, concerning the augmentation <term>augmentation | also called multiplication; the process of increasing the quantity or potency of the alchemical Stone</term> of our Great Stone, I will present and make known to you through a parable.

<term>Antimony</term> <note>original: "Spießglaß"; stibnite or antimony ore, highly valued in alchemy for its purifying properties.</note>

<margin><image-desc>A hand-drawn triangle or delta symbol.</image-desc></margin>Just as it is difficult for a master builder to fully master the compass, since the <note>original: "Architectus Jehova"</note> Divine Architect Jehovah has reserved much art for Himself; so too is <term>antimony</term> difficult to fully research in all its secrets. For its virtue is wonderful and its power mighty; the color hidden within it is manifold. Its raw body is poisonous, but its <term>essence</term> <note>original: "Essentia"; the concentrated inward nature or "soul" of a substance.</note> resists poison, much like <term>mercury</term> <note>original: "Quecksilber"</note>. This is something the inexperienced physician cannot grasp or find, but the knowledgeable physician believes it through the revelation of manifold proof.

<margin><image-desc>Faint handwritten annotations or scribbles, possibly numerical.</image-desc></margin>This mineral has much <term>mercury</term> <note>original: "Mercurium"; the "spirit" or volatile principle in the Tria Prima theory.</note>, also much <term>sulfur</term> <note>original: "Schwebel"; the "soul" or combustible principle.</note>, and little <term>salt</term> <note>original: "Saltz"; the "body" or solid principle.</note>; therefore it is brittle and unyielding. For malleability is not found in it because of the small quantity of its salt. Its greatest affinity, because of its mercury, is for <term>Saturn</term> <note>original: "Saturno"; the planetary name for lead.</note>, for the <term>Lead of the Philosophers</term> <note>original: "Bley der Philosophen"; a specialized alchemical substance, not common lead, used as a starting material for the Great Work.</note> is made from it. But because of its sulfur, it is related to <term>gold</term>, for it purifies gold <note>Antimony was used in metallurgical "trials" to separate gold from other metals.</note> and leaves nothing evil with it. The same effect is found in it when it is used for humans after its preparation. It flies away entirely in the fire, and yet remains stable in the fire, provided a proper <term>process</term> <note>original: "Proceß"; a specific sequence of chemical operations.</note> is established and carried out. Its flying spirit is poisonous and purges with distress <note>original: "Beschwerung"; likely referring to the violent vomiting or physical "burden" caused by unrefined antimony.</note>—

## On Common Sulfur.

Commonly used sulfur is not yet exalted to such a perfect degree, nor brought to such ripeness, as it is found in antimony <term>Spießglaß<gloss>stibnite or antimony ore, which alchemists believed contained a more "mature" or "pure" sulfur than the common yellow variety</gloss></term> and vitriol. Now, an oil is made from it by itself <note>original: "per se"</note> for foul, stinking wounds; it also kills the worms that grow therein, especially if the salt of sulfur (the quantity of which is very small) has been dissolved in it.

A balsam is also made from it with tree or juniper oil, as well as with the white spirit of turpentine. It is red in color, and this occurs when the flowers of sulfur <term>flores des Schwefels<gloss>the fine powder produced when sulfur is sublimated by heat</gloss></term> are prepared through a *colcothar* of vitriol <term>Colchotar des Vitrioli<gloss>the red iron oxide residue remaining after the distillation of vitriol; used here as a catalyst or medium</gloss></term> and digested for a time in horse dung <note>A common alchemical method for providing a gentle, consistent heat over several weeks</note> or otherwise. This same balsam is good to use internally for those suffering from lung disease <note>original: "Lungensüchtigen"; likely referring to consumption or tuberculosis</note>, especially if it is first rectified several times with the spirit of wine <note>distilled alcohol</note>, drawn over, and separated until it has become blood-red; for this balsam preserves against decay.

# Of Arsenic <term>Arsenico<gloss>A brittle, gray metalloid, notorious in alchemy for its volatility and its role in "whitening" metals</gloss></term>.

Arsenic is related to Mercury <term>Mercurio<gloss>Quicksilver</gloss></term> and Antimony <term>Antimonio<gloss>A semi-metal used to purify gold</gloss></term> much like a bastard <term>Banckhard<gloss>Literally "bench-hard," a term for an illegitimate child; here used metaphorically to describe a substance that shares chemical traits with metals but is not a "true" metal</gloss></term> in its kinship; poisonous and volatile in its entire being, just like the previous two. In its color, it is outwardly in its manifestation white, yellow, and red; inwardly, it is adorned with all colors, just like its metals, which it was forced to leave through the compulsion of fire. It is sublimated <term>sublimirt<gloss>The process of heating a substance so it turns to vapor and then solidifies again, skipping the liquid phase</gloss></term> by itself without additives, and also with additives in many ways. However, when it is driven upward through salt and Mars <term>Martem<gloss>The alchemical name for iron</gloss></term>, it appears as transparent as a crystal. But its poison is still within it, and it is not at all fit to be added to metals, as the smallest quantity is to be found in it to change metals. <note>This suggests that while arsenic can change the appearance of metals, its "poisonous" or volatile nature makes it unsuitable for stable transmutation in this state.</note>

If a person is possessed by blindness, they cannot pass judgment on any writing; but understanding judges with patience, and wisdom separates itself from folly through its own experience.

The *vital spirit* <note>original: Spiritus vitalis</note> or the living spirit in man is mobile; it wanders through all his limbs and is sensitive within them, yet incomprehensible. If it is withdrawn from any limb by accident, that limb becomes deadly [lifeless], and can in no other way have life or movement or any feeling again, unless it be *restored* <note>original: restituirt</note> and brought back to its former state through proper means and the help of medicine.

This *vital spirit* now nourishes, feeds, and maintains itself solely from the richness of the human sulfur <note>original: Schwefels; in alchemy, sulfur represents the combustible, oily principle of life and heat</note>, which reigns in the blood and acts through it upon the entire body, so that it may be a complete being.

For the *vital spirit* is the *Mercury* <note>original: Mercurius</note> found within man, which sustains itself from the richness of its own kind. Thus there are now two: *Mercury* and *Sulfur*. Whatever else is found in man—namely in the remaining flesh, body, and bone—there is also found <term>Salt; the third of the "Tria Prima" or three primary substances (Salt, Sulfur, Mercury) believed by alchemists to constitute all matter</term> as the third part.

The <term>Salt</term> now gives its most noble <term>spirit; original: Spiritum</term> as nourishment to the blood—this saltiness can even be tasted within it—and distributes itself from there into the whole body. It preserves the human body like a balsam against all decay and acts as a bond and <term>union; original: copulation</term>, so that the *Mercury* or *vital spirit* may remain longer with the balsam in the flesh and dwell together as one.

# ON THE MICROCOSM <note>original Latin: "De Microcosmo"</note>

Thus, one nature follows after another, unfathomable and incomprehensible. For the time being, it remains unknown to the common man—who is not concerned with learning the ways of nature—and is even regarded by him as quite unbelievable.

But to speak again of man: the noblest spirit of life has its dominion and dwelling most strongly in the heart of the human body, as the most noble place. The <term>Sulfur of man; original Latin: "Sulphur hominis"; the oily, soul-like principle of heat and growth</term> provides such a spirit with nourishment and a spiritual pathway for its preservation through the air. For when air is taken away from a person, the spirit of life must suffocate and departs invisibly, and thus the death of the human has already appeared. 

The noblest <term>Salt-spirit; original: "Salȝ-Geift"; the alchemical principle of stability and preservation</term>, however, is a preserver of both <note>referring to the sulfur and the spirit of life</note>. Its noblest spirit permeates everything, but the coarsest matter of its salt is cast off into the bladder. This substance, however, possesses a <term>spirit; original Latin: "Spiritum"</term> of a particular kind and operation. And whatever of the salt passes out through the bladder, heat acts upon it again and provides a new gateway, so that the supply of salt in man is inexhaustible until he passes away entirely, his body is burnt to ash, and the remaining <term>residue; original Latin: "residuum"</term> is extracted. 

Take a similar example from all the <term>salts of minerals; original: "Salȝ der Mineralien"</term>, which grow again through heat, <term>coagulate; thicken or solidify</term>, and allow themselves to be extracted through <term>wateriness; original: "Wäfserigkeit"</term>. In particular, all common salts and <term>saltpeter; a mineral salt (potassium nitrate) used in alchemy and gunpowder</term> earth provide certainty of this, and thus further examples are judged unnecessary at this time.

I can truly bring you no more than this,
For Sun and Moon are not within me. <note>original: Sol und Luna. In the symbolic language of alchemy, Sun refers to Gold and Moon refers to Silver. The author is stating that Sal Ammoniac contains no precious metals itself.</note>

## COMMON SALT <note>original: SAL COMMUNE. Ordinary table salt (sodium chloride), used in alchemy for purification and "fixing" other spirits.</note>

A wonderful balsam am I,
What is clearly found in the Eagle, <gloss>Sal Ammoniac</gloss> <note>The "Eagle" was a common alchemical code name for Sal Ammoniac because the salt "flies" (sublimes) when heated.</note>
Also dwells within me, quite the same;
Otherwise, I make no metals rich,
Except that I break them alone,
Purge and cleanse their kind, <note>Salt was used in various "cementation" processes to remove impurities from gold and silver.</note>
Also draw from them color and tincture,
Provided I am sweet and not at all sour;
The spirit of wine causes me fear and woe, <note>original: Weingeist. Distilled alcohol. The "woe" refers to the chemical reaction or precipitation that occurs when these substances meet.</note>
This produces Potable Gold. <term>Aurum potabile: "Drinkable gold," a legendary medicine made by dissolving gold into a liquid form. It was believed to grant longevity and cure all ailments.</term>

## SALTPETER <note>original: SALPETER. Saltpeter (potassium nitrate), a primary ingredient in gunpowder and the production of nitric acid.</note>

A wonder-salt am I on earth,
My like will hardly ever be seen;
Without me, one can accomplish almost nothing,
I must help to settle all matters.

## T A R T A R <note>original: TARTARUS. Also known as "Cream of Tartar" or potassium bitartrate, this salt forms as a sediment in wine barrels.</note>

I call myself "Vegetable," <note>Alchemy categorized substances as Mineral, Animal, or Vegetable. Tartar is "vegetable" because it originates from the juice of the grape.</note>

The Venus-star is my name,

### Of the Birth of Saturn <note>original: "Saturni"; the Latin genitive form of Saturn. In alchemy, Saturn represents the metal lead and the beginning of the "Great Work."</note>.

# The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom. <note>original Latin: "Initium ſapientiæ eſt timor Domini," a common biblical opening for alchemical texts to signal that spiritual piety is a prerequisite for success in the laboratory.</note>

Now hereafter is set the table <note>This likely refers to a diagram or schematic that would have followed this text in the original manuscript.</note> wherein the beginning, the middle, and the end—regarded as the right, true foundation of all **philosophical wisdom**—is contained. Within it, the highest **medicine** for health, long-lasting age, and the wealth of human life is briefly and summarily contained.

->Beginning, middle, and the end,<-
->All stands in God’s hand;<-
->Health, wealth, and long life<-
->He alone can give to us all.<-

The Almighty and eternal **God**, whose beginning has no end, and whose wisdom has been from the start and stems from eternity, has created out of His inscrutable counsel heaven and earth, and all that is contained therein, visible and invisible, whatever name it may or can have, out of nothing but emanated power. He accomplished everything through a single word, that which Divine Wisdom through her Divine Being had decreed in eternal counsel; and that word was **"Let it be done"** <note>original Latin: "FIAT"</note>. Following this, God has henceforth given to **Nature**—through which she can further work, multiply, and generate—a natural birth and joining, so that through the action and help of one another, all things are brought forth.

<term>Creation</term>, <term>"Let it be done"</term> <note>original: FIAT</note>, <term>Philosophical Wisdom</term> <note>In this context, "philosophy" refers to Alchemy, the study of the hidden laws of nature.</note>, <term>Medicine</term>, <term>Nature</term>

<summary>This page establishes the theological foundation of alchemy, asserting that all physical transformation and the "highest medicine" (the Philosopher's Stone) originate from God's initial act of creation. It frames nature as a divinely ordained system of generation and growth that the alchemist must follow.</summary>

# Of the natural [processes]

...in which he can rest and work; and this Spirit is found in all metals, and more abundantly in other metals than in gold. For gold, on account of its boiled-up, well-ripened, fixed body, is dense, firm, and compact. Therefore, no more can enter into the body than what the body <term>Corpus: the physical, material substance of a metal.</term> requires. The other metals, however, do not have such a fixed body; rather, their pores are open and widely distributed. For this reason, the Spirit of the Tincture <note>The Tincture is the transformative "soul" or essence that alchemists believed could change one substance into another.</note> can more abundantly pass through and occupy them. But because the bodies of the other metals are unstable <note>original: "unbeständig" — referring to metals that oxidize or melt easily compared to gold.</note>, the Tincture cannot remain with these unstable bodies, but must depart.

Accordingly, since the Tincture of gold is found in none more abundantly than in Mars <note>original: "Marte" — Iron</note> and Venus <note>original: "Venere" — Copper</note>, as Man and Woman, their bodies are destroyed and their Tincture-Spirit is driven out of them. This makes the "opened-up" gold rich in blood and, through its "food and drink" <note>Metaphors for the chemical additives or solvents used in the alchemical process to "nourish" the reaction.</note>, volatile. For this reason, once the volatile gold has been satiated with its food and drink, it takes its own blood unto itself and dries out through its own internal heat, with the help and addition of the vaporous fire. This results in a further overcoming <note>A stage of refinement where the substance becomes even more stable and potent.</note>, which makes it entirely fixed and of the highest stability, so that the gold becomes a "super-fixed" Medicine <note>original: "Medicin" — in alchemy, the "Medicine" or "Elixir" is the perfected Stone used to "heal" or transform base metals into gold.</note>. 

On account of this "excessive blood," it cannot provide a body unless an additional metallic body is added to it, into which the surplus fixed blood can distribute itself. This added metallic body—because of the great heat of the fixed Lion's Blood <note>original: "Löwen-Blut" — a potent alchemical symbol for the red, transformative essence of the Philosopher's Stone at its most powerful stage.</note>—is passed through like a fire, cleansed of all impurity, and instantly boiled out into a complete ripeness and fixity. # The Fourth Chapter.
## Concerning the Spirit of Copper.

The star of Venus is difficult and not easily calculated—as all mathematicians and astronomers <note>original: *Mathematici und Astronomi*</note> must prove to me—for its course has a different character than what is found among the other six planets. Therefore, its birth is also of a different nature, because the birth of Venus <note>original: *Veneris*</note> occupies the first table after Mercury <note>original: *Mercurio*</note>, as far as the birth of metals is concerned. Mercury makes active, but Venus entices and provides pleasure and desire together with beauty, which provide the cause for it. Although I do not consider myself an astronomer, nor do I pass myself off as one who is aware of the calculations of the heavenly course—because I am to spend my time in my house of God with prayer—yet so that the remaining time after performing my devotions may not pass in vain, I have set my goal and undertaken to practice and fully accomplish myself in the experience of natural things. 

Thus, it is also not easily calculated what arises, grows, and comes from Venus, or from what she has arisen, grown, and come, because she is superfluously clothed in what she herself does not need, and conversely must lack that which she would well need for constancy <note>In alchemy, "constancy" or "fixity" refers to a metal's ability to withstand fire without evaporating or corroding; copper is famously "unfixed" compared to gold</note>.

<margin>A</margin>ctivity <note>original: *Actur*; referring to the active principle or power of a substance</note> is handed down in verdigris; it is also found in vitriol <note>a sulfate mineral</note> as a mineral, about which an entire book could be written. The right, true sulfur, however, is incombustible, for it is a pure, true **spirit** <note>original: *Spiritus*</note>, from which the **incombustible oil** <note>original: *Oleum incombustibile*; a legendary alchemical substance that remains unchanged by fire</note> is prepared; and it is this very sulfur from which the gold-sulfur was made and produced from a root.

I am revealing many secrets that perhaps should not be told; but what should I do? To remain silent about everything is also not responsible. Yet, moderation is good in all things, as you must take note of in my last report of the protestation <note>a formal declaration or statement of principles</note>, where you will not forget my request.

This sulfur may well be called and baptized the **Sulfur of all Sages**, because all wisdom is found in it, right down to the **mercurial spirit** <note>original: *Mercurial-Geist*</note> that precedes it and exists simultaneously with it. Together with the **salt of Mars** <note>original: *Sal Marti*; typically referring to iron sulfate or the essence of iron</note>, it must be put together through spiritual union, so that the three attain a single understanding and are raised into the same effect.

By this, the stars demonstrate a separation between **fixed** and **unfixed** <note>stable or volatile when heated</note>, and between colored and uncolored things.

->For the fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom.<-

# Triumphal Chariot

...to set **Antimony** <term>Antimony: original *Antimonium*; a metallic mineral that alchemists believed held the secret to universal medicine once its "poison" was removed.</term> in its proper place, in order to ground its essence and to explore and investigate its ultimate science through diligence. As an example: when a craftsman wishes to prepare and brew a **beer** from barley, wheat, or other grain, he must first pass through all these **stages** <note>original: "Gradus"</note> perfectly before he can force out the noblest power and **essence** <note>original: "Essenß"</note> and bring it to a potent drink. Following this, the dried, prepared fruit is poured into the mill, crushed small, and ground, which is now its vegetable **Calcination** <term>calcination: *Calcinatio*; the reduction of a substance to a powder or ash through heat or grinding</term>.

Every glass, no matter what it is made from, whether from metals or other things, must have a right and perfect fermentation <note>original: *Gähre*; in this context, it refers to the state of chemical maturity or "ripeness" achieved through heat</note> if it is to work correctly, attain a clear transparent appearance, and undergo further preparation into medicine <note>original: *Artzney*</note>. Once the **antimony** <note>original: **Antimonium**</note> has thus become a glass in the crucible, take a broad, flat brass basin or bowl. Warm it beforehand over the fire, otherwise it will shatter, and pour the antimony out into it as thinly as you can. This **glass** also possesses within it the best power and virtue to be effective for further preparation. I call this **glass** "the pure glass," because others are made by adding **borax** <note>original: **Borras**</note> and other substances or additives.

# Triumphal Chariot #
### of Antimony ###

... pound of **mercury** <note>original: *Quecksilber*</note>; stir it continuously with a wooden stick until it becomes a **mass** <note>original: *Massa*; a uniform chemical mixture</note>. Grind this mass small, for it has been prepared in the same manner that one usually makes **cinnabar** <note>original: *Zinnober*; mercury sulfide, a bright red mineral</note>. Grind into it four ounces of **antimony** <term>Spießglas</term>, four ounces of red **arsenic** <term>Arsenicum</term>, two ounces of **saffron of Mars** <term>Crocum Martis</term> <note>iron oxide, often used to impart a red color or for its supposed strengthening properties</note>, and eight ounces of brick dust. Put all these pieces together into a glass flask and **sublimate** them <note>the process of heating a substance until it vaporizes and then solidifies again in the cooler upper part of the vessel</note>, following the manual techniques customary for such matters. In this sublimation, you will obtain **rubies** <note>red crystals formed through the chemical reaction, resembling the gemstone but purely chemical in nature</note> that are in no way inferior to those from the Orient, but only regarding their color; for they have no **fixity** <note>original: *Fixigkeit*; the ability of a substance to remain stable and not evaporate when exposed to high heat</note>, but are entirely **volatile** <note>original: *flüchtig*</note> and fly away quickly in the fire.

These rubies are then separated from the **cinnabar** that also rose during the sublimation; the artist should grind them small and extract them with a sharp, distilled **wine vinegar**. When such work is done, draw off the vinegar in a **water bath** <term>Balneo Mariæ</term> very gently; thus a powder remains behind. This same powder is ground small once again, as before, placed into another glass, and extracted a second time with a **spirit of wine** <term>Spiritu vini</term> <note>concentrated alcohol or ethanol used as a solvent</note>. Thus the **dregs** <note>original: *fæces*; the insoluble waste material left at the bottom</note> remain behind and are separated from it. This **extraction** <note>original: *extractio*</note> with the spirit of wine, well-sealed in a glass, should be **digested** <note>kept at a gentle, steady warmth to encourage chemical integration</note> very gently in a **water bath** <term>Frauen-Bad</term> <note>literally "Lady's Bath," a synonym for the Balneum Mariae or water bath</note> for one month. Finally, draw off the **spirit of wine** <note>original: *Spiritum des Wein*</note> from it again, as was done with the vinegar before. <margin>45</margin>
Another medicine is prepared from antimony, regarding which I have found that it has accomplished excellent and high things in fevers that have arisen, of whatever kind they may be, as well as in the time of the <term>plague</term> <note>original: *Pestilenz*</note>; namely, that the **antimony** is ground very small, then put into a glass, and thus driven over strongly with fire in a **retort** <note>original: *Retorten*; a glass vessel with a long, downward-pointing neck used for distilling or sublimating substances.</note> without any addition, for the third or fourth time, into a large receiver glass; in the end, a red powder results from it. Extract this with **vinegar** <note>original: *aceto*</note>; let this **extraction** circulate with a gentle fire for ten days long; then **distill** the vinegar away from it, and what remains must be completely driven over into an **oil** <note>original: *oleum*</note> by a special manual technique. This oil is further circulated and **pelicanized** <note>original: *pellicanirt*; a process of continuous distillation where the condensed liquid flows back into the main body of the flask, named after the "pelican" vessel which resembles the bird pecking its own breast.</note> until the moisture has left it and it has once again become a powder—after the vinegar was initially separated from it through **distillation** and the final **oil** was caught in a new receiver.

Taking four grains of this oil with a **distilled water of Blessed Thistle** <note>original: *Cardebenedicten*; a plant historically used in monastic medicine to treat fevers and infections.</note> and being warmly covered thereafter, and sweating well upon it, cures the second, third, and fourth-day **fevers** <note>The author refers here to "tertian" and "quartan" fevers, which were characterized by the intervals of days between paroxysms.</note>. Used in the same weight with a **spirit of wine** <note>original: *Spiritu vini*; high-proof alcohol.</note> or a distilled wine vinegar—depending on whether the plague initially showed itself with chills or heat—it has been found to have remarkable virtue in driving the same away. This was seen in our monastery when three of my fellow brothers, who at the same time were nearly surrendered to death by such a plague and had entirely [concluded] their last wills...

<header>Triumphal Chariot</header>

<margin>48</margin>
The water was commanded to stand still, and there opened a great depth within a very high mountain, which I afterwards entered. I wished to see therein whether it were possible—as the children of men say—that there might be a friendship and communion between the Upper and the Lower <note>A reference to the famous Hermetic maxim "As above, so below," suggesting that the heavens and the earth reflect one another.</note>, and also whether the upper stars had received such power from their Creator to work their likeness within the Earth.

<margin>64</margin>
As I gathered all this information, I found so much that it was truly, and in the highest and greatest truth, everything that the old teachers <term>Præceptores</term> <note>original: *Præceptores*; Latin for "preceptors" or "teachers," referring here to the ancient masters of alchemy.</note> had long ago written and left behind for their disciples and students who truly desire to follow them and establish a foundation. For this, I give high thanks to my Almighty Lord of Heaven <note>original: *Himmel-HErrn*</note>, as is only right, with heart and mouth for His unfathomable wonders.

<margin>41?</margin>
I discovered briefly, however, that all internal mountain-growths <term>Berg-Gewächse</term> <note>original: *Berg-Gewächse*; the alchemical belief that minerals and metals "grow" in the earth like plants, nourished by celestial influences.</note> were poured out from the upper stars <note>original: *Obergestirn*</note> and take their beginning from a watery vapor <note>original: *Dampff*</note>, smoke, or watery mists <note>original: *Wasser-Schwaden*</note>. This vapor was further nourished over a long time by the stars and was made into a tangible form by the Elements <term>Elementa</term>. Through this, the vapor was dried out so that the wateriness lost its mastery, and Fire, following the Water and with the help of Air <note>original: *Lufft*</note>, gained the upper hand. Thus, at one time, fire came from water, and from fire and air came earth <note>original: *Erden*</note>. These elements are still found indistinguishably in all things of the world before their separation <note>The alchemical process of "Separatio," where a substance is broken down into its core elemental components.</note> within every physical body.

# Triumphal Chariot
<meta>catchword: toward-</meta>

Love surpasses all other infirmities and diseases, for it can in no way be helped except through a remedy of its own kind <note>The author alludes to the homeopathic principle of "like cures like," suggesting that the "disease" of love can only be cured by the object of that love.</note>, which is the desire of both natures. This is only extinguished through the fulfillment of the will of that ignited and captured longing. Even in this current hour, many must testify to what love can do; for it does not only look upon the young, but also the old, who burn entirely, rave, and rage so much in their old age because of love that they become complete fools on its account.

Other natural diseases also regulate themselves according to the **complexion** <term>Complexion: In early modern medicine, this refers to an individual's "temperament" or the specific balance of the four humors (blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile) within their body</term> of the person, affecting one individual more violently than another. Love, however, makes no distinction whatsoever; rather, when it arrives, it strikes equally through rich and poor, old and young people alike, and fears no snare, no matter how wicked it may be.

<margin><unclear>S. M. P.</unclear></margin>
In other natural weaknesses and ailments, a person feels only certain limbs that suffer pain and have been overtaken by it, while the remaining limbs meanwhile enjoy rest and peace. But love infects and takes over the entire body, with its entire **substance** <term>Substance: The essential physical reality of the body, as opposed to its mere outward appearance</term>, being, and form—nothing is excluded in the slightest. For the heart is so filled with **ardor** <term>Ardor: (German: *Brunst*) a state of intense heat or passionate burning, often used in alchemical texts to describe the "hunger" one substance has for another</term> that a distribution follows into all the veins and limbs of the entire body. And so I say: when love is rightly rooted, it takes away all **reason** <term>Reason: (German: *Vernunfft*) the faculty of logic and moral judgment, which the author argues is completely overwhelmed by the "heat" of passion</term>, sense, and thoughts, and the person wanders to such an extent that they forget everything—

<summary>The author compares the power of love to a disease, noting that unlike localized illnesses, love consumes the entire body, mind, and reason regardless of a person's age or status. This serves as a macrocosmic analogy for the powerful "attractions" or chemical affinities between substances in the alchemical process.</summary>
<keywords>love, disease, complexion, humors, ardor, reason, human nature, anatomy of passion</keywords>

## of Antimony.

...sets aside and risks everything, thinking neither of **God**, His Word, nor His promise, much less of His wrath, threats, and punishment (I am speaking here specifically of when a disorderly, forbidden love has been ignited). In short, the person does not allow themselves to be turned away or held back; they forget their office, calling, and **condition** <term>Condition: A person's social status, rank, or professional standing.</term>. They regard all faithful warnings as mockery; they take no heed of the words of parents, authorities, or other well-meaning people who have their best interests at heart, nor do they grant them any hearing. Thus, love deprives many of their sight to such a degree that they cannot recognize their own misfortune. *Also* <note>original: "Item"</note>, it makes them deaf, so that their hearing is entirely closed off against all those who faithfully warn them of damage to both body and soul.

Love also deprives many people of their natural sleep, so that they can rest neither day nor night; likewise, it takes away the **appetite** <term>Appetite: The natural desire for food and drink.</term> and pleasure in eating. Many times, due to the anxiety, martyrdom, and torment of love, they can neither eat nor drink. Some also abandon their calling and trade, leaving everything as it lies, thinking of no work, neither reading nor studying, and only run after vain love.

Many also fall into great **distress** <term>Distress: From the German 'Beschwerung', meaning a heavy burden or affliction of the spirit.</term>, sadness, and **melancholy thoughts** <term>Melancholy thoughts: In the 17th century, 'melancholy' was considered a physical ailment caused by an imbalance of the humors, leading to deep sadness and obsessive fixation.</term>, especially when things do not go as they would wish according to their own mind. But the person heeds none of this, and [strives]...

Everyone should know, however, that our stone, called *Fire* <note>original: "Ignis"</note>, must be boiled and brought to maturity by physical fire within the Little World <note>The "Microcosmus" or Little World refers to the human sphere and the alchemist's laboratory, which mirrors the "Macrocosmus" or the universe at large.</note>, just as other foods and medicines must be prepared. Wheat is increased and ripened by the elemental fire of the Great World <note>The natural heat of the sun and the seasons.</note>; however, it is only through the physical fire of the Little World <note>Human arts, such as cooking or baking.</note> that another new boiling and ripening is accomplished, so that humans can further use that blessing for their own sustenance. In this way, the last and smallest thing—which was produced from the great and first thing—can fulfill its purpose.

The true *Oil of Antimony* <note>original: "oleum Antimonii"; a potent chemical extract believed to have profound medicinal and alchemical properties.</note>, from which the stone called *Fire* is prepared, possesses an exceedingly great and sweet quality. It is separated and purified from its earth <note>original: "terra"; the solid residue or dross remaining after distillation or extraction.</note> in such a way that if a small vial of it is placed in the sun, it casts out many diverse and wonderful rays. It is as if countless fiery mirrors were present in a room or chamber, gleaming ruby-red and with many other marvelous colors.

Now listen, my dear seeker of the Art, you who love the truth and intend to learn something, and are eager to discover more:

Take, in the name of the Most High, Antimony <note>original: "Spießglaß"; the historical name for the mineral stibnite, the primary ore of antimony.</note>.

# of Antimony. 451

<margin><unclear>scribble</unclear> 342</margin>
Take one part ore that has grown toward the sunrise <note>Alchemical symbolism suggesting ore from the east or ore of a specific ripeness.</note>, and one part Saltpeter <note>Potassium nitrate, a powerful oxidizing agent in early chemistry.</note> that is good and pure; grind it all small and mix it together; then place it in a moderate fire; burn or calcine <note>original: "glües"; to heat a substance to a high temperature without melting it to change its chemical properties.</note> it together according to the manual technique which is the masterpiece; then a substance remains which is inclined toward a brown color. Turn that substance into a glass <note>A vitrified or translucent material produced by high heat.</note>; grind that same glass small again, and extract the deep red **tincture** <note>original: "Tinctur"; a concentrated extract or essence.</note> from it with a pure, good, and sharp distilled vinegar made from its own mineral. Draw off the vinegar through **distillation** in a **water bath** <note>original: "Balneo Mariæ"; a double-boiler method providing gentle, indirect heat.</note>, so that a powder remains behind. Extract that powder once more with **spirit of wine** <note>original: "Spiritu vini"; concentrated alcohol or ethanol.</note> brought to its highest purity; then the dregs <note>original: "feces"; the solid residue or sediment.</note> remain behind, and you have an exceedingly beautiful red **extraction**, sweet and lovely, which is highly useful to use in medicine.

<margin>454</margin>
That is now the pure **Sulfur of Antimony** <note>original: "Sulphur Antimonii"; in alchemy, 'sulfur' represents the active, soulful, or flammable principle of a substance.</note>, separated to the highest degree. If you have 2 pounds of this extraction, then take eight *Lot* <note>A historical unit of weight, approximately 1/32nd of a pound or 15 grams.</note> of **Salt of Antimony** <note>original: "Salis Antimonii"; the 'body' or crystalline essence of the substance.</note>, as I have taught you to make; pour this extraction onto it and circulate <note>A process of continuous distillation and condensation in a closed vessel, often called refluxing today.</note> it well together for at least one month, well sealed, so the salt will have united itself with the extraction of sulfur. If it has deposited dregs, then separate them from it, and first distill the **spirit of wine** from it in the **bath of the Holy Virgin Mary** <note>A pious name for the water bath or *Balneum Mariae*.</note>. The powder that remains for the artist, drive with a strong fire; then, with great and unbelievable wonder, many colors pass over, and a lovely sweet **oil** <note>original: "oleum"</note> comes across, completely transparent and red in its dissolution. Rectify <note>To purify a liquid by repeated distillation.</note> this oil once more in a **water bath** until the fourth part of it comes over; then it is <margin><unclear>regent</unclear></margin> right.

Second (1) Part

## Preface and Introduction

# BROTHER BASIL VALENTINE,

->Of the Benedictine Order.<-

Since the time is at hand that I, by the will of God my Creator and His dear Son Jesus Christ, must close my laboratory <note>Basil Valentine uses the "laboratory" as both a physical space for alchemical work and a spiritual metaphor for the human life where the soul is refined.</note> here in this transitory world, and proceed from day to day—indeed, from hour to hour—to appeal from that same earthly laboratory to the true heavenly one; and since the end is near to conclude my life through the appointed goal of the supreme throne of grace <note>original: "Gnadenthron"; a biblical reference to the mercy seat or the presence of God where one receives grace.</note> of Jesus Christ; and as I daily sigh and carry a heartfelt longing for the true bread of heaven <note>original: "Himmelbrod"; referring to spiritual nourishment and eternal life.</note> of eternal salvation, where riches and everlasting joy are in abundance and without end: it has also seemed fitting to me, and I have felt and considered it in my conscience as highly necessary, to establish a Christian reconciliation with my fellow Christians, those now living in this world and those to come after me. I do this so that my soul, in the peace and patience of the summons of my dear God, may await the Heavenly Paradise and dwelling, and remain in readiness day and night to be inscribed in the Book of Life. By which

<sig>A</sig>
<meta>catchword: He.</meta>

<summary>In this solemn preface, the author, writing as the monk Basil Valentine, prepares for his death by framing his alchemical life as a spiritual "laboratory" and seeking reconciliation with his readers.</summary>
<keywords>Basil Valentine, Benedictine, laboratory, salvation, throne of grace, bread of heaven, reconciliation, Book of Life, alchemy, deathbed testament</keywords>

--- Page 568 ---
<meta>This page continues the preface of Brother Basil Valentine. On the previous page, the author expressed his desire to make peace with his fellow Christians and prepare his soul for death. This page transitions into his motivation for sharing his alchemical secrets: a sense of duty and compassion for those struggling in spiritual and physical "darkness."</meta>

In this consideration, I simultaneously recall all my writings which I have previously recorded and published—just as the Ancients did before me. Although neither compulsion nor pressure has been placed upon me—and much less have I been incited by my own fame or vanity to write down and leave behind even a single letter—I have nevertheless considered the misery and wretchedness of this world, in which the children of obscurity and darkness have fallen; indeed, they are almost completely perishing.

### Brother Basil Valentine.

Oh God, how my spirit is troubled when I consider the folly of this contemptible world and the blindness of all its children—who nevertheless consider themselves noble and wise, having attended **universities** <note>original: "hohen Schulen"; literally "high schools," referring to the scholastic institutions of the time, which Valentine frequently criticized for favoring book-learning over practical experience.</note>, and imagining they have gathered great understanding within their minds. Where has the high and precious medicine of the ancient, wise masters flown—those who lived before any university was even built or invented? They received their revelation solely through heartfelt, pleading prayer to God and through daily investigation and **manual labor** <note>original: "HandArbeit"; a technical term in alchemy referring to the practical, physical operations performed in a laboratory, such as distillation and calcination.</note>. Where, I ask, has their toil and labor vanished? Nowhere else than in the old, cavernous, unclean, and moldy apothecary shops, plunged deep into the earth and buried—indeed, completely sunken, such that they cannot be awakened again by any **sound of the mortar** <note>original: "Mörsel-klang"; the rhythmic sound of a pestle in a mortar, the traditional symbol of the pharmacist's craft.</note> to further spread and demonstrate their praise with wonder and with the glorification of the Most High.

But I know for certain that when my writings properly come to light and appear before the day after my death, and are rightly read, contemplated, and understood by wise descendants, apostles, and disciples of wisdom—and are furthermore sought and worked upon with a Christian purpose, for no other reason than the glory of God and the love of one’s fellow Christian—that through such right and well-founded labor, all the bumbling and bungling of those supposed, boastful, vainglorious fellows and high-flown fools will be [exposed]. These are the ones who describe themselves and present themselves as physicians and masters of **both medicines** <note>original: "beyder Artzneyen"; likely referring to the Paracelsian concept of medicine for both the internal body and external wounds, or the medicine of both the body and the spirit.</note>—that is, writing of things internal and external—and who desire to be held in high honor for it...

Although it does not belong here [to discuss] how <term>minerals and fossils</term> <note>original: "mineralia fossilia"; in this period, "fossil" referred to anything "dug up" from the earth, including ores</note> are made under the earth / yet Nature works and makes them from the earth's moist juices / and <term>mountain waxes</term> <note>original: "Bergwaxen"; naturally occurring bitumens or mineral resins found in mines</note> / these same are thereafter the food of the metals / not those processed <note>original: "gesottenen"; literally "boiled," referring here to metals that have already been smelted or refined</note> substances mentioned above; therefore, if you wished to add such processed substances in their physical form without being dissolved into your further work with metals / you will labor in vain / and wherever such minerals are found / there are also mines / if not close by / then certainly not far away / all mines demonstrate this / as in Hungary there are the most beautiful / and best / Sulfur, Alum, and Vitriol.

### CHAPTER V.
# ON THE EGRESS AND INGRESS of Metals,
<note>original: *DE EGRESSIONE ET INGRESSIONE Metallorum*</note>
->or<-
## On the Exit and Entry of Metals.

<margin>16.</margin>
The work of metals testifies to a constant exiting and entering of the metals; for by "exit" one should understand not only the departure of the entire work—whereby a mine in one place completely perishes when it has nothing left to consume and has exhausted <unclear>all</unclear> of its own bodies <note>original: *corpora*</note>—but also the partial exit. For one [part] always seeks the other and follows closely on its heels. You can see this clearly in metallic mercury <note>original: *Mercurio metallo*</note> when you pour it out: how it divides itself into many hundreds of small, lively grains, which nevertheless all flow back together into one body <note>original: *corpus*</note>. The volatile and the slippery <note>original: *volatile uñ lubricum*</note> behave in this same way. But the <term>Ferch</term> <note>An archaic mining term referring to the "vital sap" or life-force of the ore, believed to give the rock its metallic value</note> also exits piece by piece in this manner, until it finally comes together in one place. And just as bees meet one another, so the <term>Ferch</term> does from one piece to another, until it comes together again in a certain place, as much of it as is necessary; for it tolerates no more than it requires. The rest and the remainder thus swarms out and into another workshop <note>Refers to a different geological vein or cavity where ore forms</note>. Such division then results in many and various kinds of mines, depending on how the workshop and the nourishment <note>original: *Speise*, referring to the mineral-rich fluids that "feed" the growth of metals</note> are prepared, and according to how one also encounters it in his work, during the exit.

### CHAPTER VIII.
## ON THE BREATHING METAL.
->or<-
# Of the Living Ore.

Since, however, through the work of mining one makes an intrusion into nature, one also obtains many kinds of metal; therefore, one must make a distinction between them, so that one might not suffer loss or waste in the labor. For just as each has its particular name and property in the work, so it also has its particular [method of] labor; it also allows itself to be found in a special way, and even to be detected with the [divining] rod. For knowing how to distinguish the metal by its colors is indeed a fine knowledge—such as red-gold ore <note>original: *Rohtgülden*; a silver ore now known as pyrargyrite</note>, vitreous ore <note>original: *Glaß-Ertz*; silver glance or acanthite</note>, green, or black ore, etc. Yet, nonetheless, one does not yet know its [manner of] processing quite thoroughly. For this reason, the [divining] rod also strikes upon the upper metals <note>original: *metalla*</note>, and that is the greatest advantage. # The 8th Chapter of the 1st Book.

...draws out with its life-blood <term>life-blood: *Ferch* is an archaic term for the soul or the vital fluid of life, often used in old mining texts to describe the "living" essence of the ore</term> and seed. And observe when a metal dies away from its perfection back into another body <note>original: *corpus*</note>; it happens just like with a human who loses their bodily color, and thereafter also their body—that is, weight. Thus, gold does not turn into "golden silver" but into an electrum <note>original: *electro*; a naturally occurring alloy of gold and silver</note>, that is, into a <unclear>C-</unclear> which has lost its color.

This is a great little assay-piece <term>assay-piece: *Probier-stücklein* is a small sample used by a metallurgist or "assayer" to test the quality and composition of a metal</term> by which one may recognize such silver-gold <note>original: *Silber-G-*</note> from true silver; for it will be found to be heavier than other silver, because it still possesses the body <note>original: *corpus*</note> and has only lost the color.

It is an even finer trick of the art that one can reawaken, restore, and give back the dead color to the body. In short, in the process of parting <note>original: *Scheiden*; the chemical separation of gold from silver</note>, all things retain the nature of gold <gloss>nature of gold: symbolized by ☉</gloss>. It is the same with raw silver that has lost its color and has thus likened and mingled itself with copper so that it dies within its body <note>original: *corpore*</note>. To bring this silver out of the copper again and give it back its own special color is a great art which the smelters do not know, but belongs rather to the chemical art <note>original: *Chymische Kunst*</note> and the laboratory <note>original: *laboratorium*</note>. # Of the fine Metal.

When the metal—be it in the ascending or descending <note>Refers to the alchemical cycles of refinement, where "ascending" relates to sublimation or vaporization and "descending" to precipitation or solidification</note>—is in its seven systems <note>original: *Systematibus*; likely referring to the seven stages of transformation or the seven planetary metals</note> or states, it rests and purifies itself until it finally enters into another body <note>original: *corpus*</note>. If one then encounters such an ore, that is the very purest metal that one can find and have in the world; here among our smelters, we call such a thing "super-fine." But our "super-fine," as it has been used until now, is an impure thing compared to this; for if it lacks even a small grain <term>grain: a traditional, tiny unit of weight used by jewelers and assayers to measure purity</term> in the refining process, it is not yet correct. Such metal is now, as one might imagine, very good and malleable, and nothing is lost during any of the work; and although one can "super-fine" all metals <note>original: *metalla*</note>, one can make none purer than Gold <note>represented by the symbol ☉</note>; for thereafter, no element attacks the gold anymore such that it could take anything from it, make a spoil <note>original: *spolio*; a loss of material or "loot" taken by the fire</note> of it, or nullify it.

The silver at Markirch <note>modern Sainte-Marie-aux-Mines</note> in Lorraine is thus super-fine and pure of all other metals; for "super-fining" actually means when a metal is pure of all other metals; for the fact that it is otherwise impure from dross <note>original: *excremento*; the waste or byproduct of the smelting process</note> can easily be remedied and does not harm its fineness. ### CHAPTER XII.
## CONCERNING THE PERFECT METAL.
<note>original Latin: *DE METALLO PERFECTO*</note>
->or<-
## Of the Perfect Metal.

Who would want to know what <term>Gold ☉</term> <note>alchemical symbol ☉</note> or <term>Silver ☽</term> <note>alchemical symbol ☽</note> were, or any other metal, if one did not recognize them in their perfection? For when they are perfect, one perceives them by their color, their weight, their malleability, their flow, and their hardness. Nature has also yielded such perfect metal entirely and completely in its native state; for beautiful, perfect, pure, and native <term>Gold ☉</term> is found in Hungary, in the white quartz, which can be broken off immediately. Likewise also silver and copper. And this is the distinction between the perfect and the pure: that the metals must first be perfect before they become pure. Therefore, there can be a perfect ore that is not pure, just as one finds such a deficiency quite often in many of our metals; for we certainly have them in a perfect state as soon as other nations do, but as for being entirely pure—that, it seems to me, we lack; may dear God help toward improvement. Thus, regarding this metal, it is noteworthy that a *body* <note>original: *corpus*; the physical substance of the metal</note> must first be perfect, or must be brought to its perfection, before it becomes <term>fixed</term> <note>original: *fix*; in alchemy, a "fixed" substance is one that can endure the fire without evaporating or changing.</note>; and much depends on this, that one rightly understands what "fixed" means.
